items.t: Eastern Hillsides is a hillside neighbourhood in southeast Chilliwack and a Neighbourhood Plan area, Schedule B4 of the Chilliwack 2050 Official Community Plan (Bylaw 2025, No. 5500). The plan was adopted in 2012, amended in 2017 to clarify development-approval requirements protecting future development from rock fall, landslide or earthflow, and updated a third time in 2025 as part of the OCP update.

Boundaries: west edge the Ryder Lake uplands, south edge Lookout Ridge and Elk Mountain, east edge the Cascade foothills / Fraser Valley Regional District boundary, and north edge the Trans-Canada Highway (Highway 1) and valley-floor farmland.
Internal roads named in City park listings include Allan Road, Rowanna Crescent and Marble Hill Road.

Where the condo stock concentrates: it does not — there is no known apartment-condo or townhome stock in this plan area at all. The established stock is freehold detached housing on individual lots, organized into development cells with unit allocations under the Neighbourhood Plan.

Anchors outside the plan area: there is no school located inside the Eastern Hillsides plan area — the Neighbourhood Plan states this directly; the nearest City recreation centre is Cheam Leisure Centre, 45501 Market Way, in Sardis; the nearest library is Chilliwack Library, 45860 First Avenue; Chilliwack General Hospital is at 45600 Menholm Road and the Chilliwack Urgent and Primary Care Centre at #104 – 7955 Evans Road, both on the valley floor.
Transit: no BC Transit route in the Chilliwack route overview runs into the Eastern Hillsides plan area; the overview lists routes 51, 52, 53, 54, 55, 57, 58, 59, 66, 71 and 72 for the city system.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect condo buyers in Eastern Hillsides

items.t: Why this section still matters with zero stock: if a strata purchase does occur here (a bare-land strata lot or a future project), BC strata housing is governed by the Strata Property Act, with disputes at the Civil Resolution Tribunal — and the standard block below is the rule set that would apply.

Form B (Strata Property Act, s.59): On any strata resale, the Form B states the unit's monthly fee, any amount owed, any special levy already approved, the CRF balance, parking and storage entitlements, and — since April 1, 2023 — a summary of the strata's insurance coverage.

Chilliwack OCP and the plan area: the current city-wide plan is the Chilliwack 2050 Official Community Plan, Bylaw 2025, No. 5500; Eastern Hillsides is its Schedule B4 Neighbourhood Plan area. The 2050 OCP update replaced the plan's land-use designations with city-wide OCP designations, while the plan's development cells and unit allocations continue to regulate how many units may be developed in the plan area.

Chilliwack zoning: Zoning Bylaw 2020, No. 5000 governs. SHR (Suburban Hillside Residential) minimum lot area is set by the bylaw's slope table and ranges from 360 m² to 990 m² (minimum lot width 12 m, depth 20 m); R3 (Small Lot Residential) minimum lot area 360 m²; HR (Hillside Residential) minimum lot area 0.2 ha with a community water system and 0.4 ha in all other cases; RH (Rural Hillside) minimum lot area 8 ha. These detached-lot minimums are why apartment form is not the form of this area. The zone applying to any specific parcel: confirm per property.

SSMUH — Chilliwack Bylaw 5395 (adopted June 18, 2024): brought the provincial small-scale multi-unit housing rules into Chilliwack's zoning. The Province granted Chilliwack an extension for part of the Proper neighbourhood and surrounding Hazel Park, with a new compliance date of December 31, 2030 — that extension area is not Eastern Hillsides, but it shows Chilliwack's SSMUH rollout is not uniform city-wide.

Hillside hazard rules — the defining rules for this area: steep slopes, main watercourses and ravines cross the plan area and the plan identifies geotechnical hazard areas; the 2017 amendments exist specifically to protect development from rock fall, landslide or earthflow, and Council directed an expanded Marble Hill development moratorium area in 2017 after continuing ground movement was reported. The City's Greenspace Plan identifies the lower and upper Marble Hill slide areas as undevelopable lands. Hillside lots are also subject to the 2050 OCP's Hillside Development Permit Area (Schedule D-5), under which a development permit is required for works including subdivision of land with 20% or greater slopes.
Chilliwack tax dates: a 5% late payment penalty is applied for taxes outstanding after July 2, 2026, and an additional 5% for taxes outstanding after August 4, 2026, per the City's property tax FAQ.

blocks.text: Good to know about Eastern Hillsides

items.t: The board boundary is a trap in this area. Chilliwack is CADREB territory, not FVREB — anyone quoting an "Eastern Hillsides median" from a SnapStats FVR report is quoting nothing, because that report has no Chilliwack section.

There is no school, recreation centre, library branch or bus route inside the plan area — the Neighbourhood Plan and the City/BC Transit listings say so directly. Every service trip goes to the valley floor or Sardis.

Marble Hill has a development moratorium history. Council directed an expanded Marble Hill development moratorium area in 2017 after continuing ground movement was reported, and the City's Greenspace Plan identifies the lower and upper Marble Hill slide areas as undevelopable lands — check whether a lot sits in the moratorium area before counting on subdivision or a build.

The plan's unit counts still govern, even though its land-use labels changed. The 2050 OCP update replaced the Neighbourhood Plan's land-use designations with city-wide designations, but the plan's development cells and unit allocations continue to regulate how many units may be developed in the plan area.

The area's parks are the amenity. City listings include Allan Creek Park (51314 Rowanna Crescent), Forest Gate Park (51442 Allan Road), Marble Hill Natural Area (7515 Marble Hill Road), Allan Creek Trail, Chilliwack Community Forest (51642 Allan Road) and the Elk Mountain Trail.

The historic wagon road is a protected heritage asset in the plan. The Neighbourhood Plan identifies the historic wagon road (Browlee Road) for protection, and states wagon roads in the area include Nixon, Ruddock, Allan and Hinkley.
Chilliwack's tax penalty is two-stepped in 2026: 5% on taxes outstanding after July 2, 2026 and a further 5% after August 4, 2026 — budget the full notice on either penalty date.

blocks.text: Lots and land in Eastern Hillsides
What trades here

items.t: Fee-simple lots are the default form: The plan describes early development as large semi-serviced lots with single-family homes, with small-lot zoning in later cells, organized into development cells with unit allocations; the established stock described in the plan is freehold detached housing on individual lots. A bare lot here is the buyer's own title — no strata corporation, no strata fee, no Form B — with zoning, the OCP, hazard rules and any geotechnical covenants on title governing instead.

Lot character, only (Zoning Bylaw 2020, No. 5000 minimums — not measured sizes): SHR (Suburban Hillside Residential) minimum lot area is set by the bylaw's slope table and ranges from 360 m² to 990 m², minimum width 12 m, depth 20 m; R3 (Small Lot Residential) 360 m², width 12 m interior / 13.5 m corner; HR (Hillside Residential) 0.2 ha with a community water system and 0.4 ha in all other cases, width 25 m; RH (Rural Hillside) 8 ha, width 25 m. The zone and slope applying to any specific parcel: confirm per property.

Serviced vs unserviced ground: the plan's own words are "large semi-serviced lots" for the early development — servicing is not uniform hillside ground. The HR zone's minimum doubling (0.2 ha with a community water system, 0.4 ha otherwise) is the bylaw's own signal that community-water status changes what a lot can be. Whether a specific lot is on community water/sewer or on well/septic: confirm with the City and on title, parcel by parcel.
Land assemblies / development sites: The plan's development cells and unit allocations are plan regulation, not for-sale assemblies — never presented here as inventory.

ALR vs non-ALR split: the plan area is hillside land above the valley floor, with valley-floor farmland along its north edge. No ALR percentage for the plan area is published, so no split figure is stated.

The hazard character of the land itself: steep slopes, main watercourses and ravines cross the plan area and the plan identifies geotechnical hazard areas; the City's Greenspace Plan identifies the lower and upper Marble Hill slide areas as undevelopable lands, and Council directed an expanded Marble Hill development moratorium area in 2017 after continuing ground movement was reported. Land value here cannot be read off lot size alone.

blocks.text: Streets, schools and getting around Eastern Hillsides

items.t: There is no school located inside the plan area — the Neighbourhood Plan states this directly. SD33 catchments are address-based through the district's School Locator; the recorded sample result for 51314 Rowanna Crescent is East Chilliwack Elementary (49190 Chilliwack Central Road), Rosedale Traditional Community School (middle) and Chilliwack Secondary.

Parks and trails serving the area: Allan Creek Park, 51314 Rowanna Crescent; Forest Gate Park, 51442 Allan Road; Marble Hill Natural Area, 7515 Marble Hill Road; Allan Creek Trail; Chilliwack Community Forest, 51642 Allan Road; and the Elk Mountain Trail. No City recreation centre and no FVRL branch is inside the plan area — nearest recreation is Cheam Leisure Centre, 45501 Market Way, Sardis, and nearest library is Chilliwack Library, 45860 First Avenue. No BC Transit route in the Chilliwack route overview runs into the plan area.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Eastern Hillsides

items.t: OCP: Chilliwack 2050, Bylaw No. 5500; Eastern Hillsides = Schedule B4: The 2050 update replaced the plan's land-use designations with city-wide OCP designations, while the plan's development cells and unit allocations continue to regulate how many units may be developed in the plan area. Under the previous OCP (Bylaw 2014, No. 4025) the Eastern Hillsides Comprehensive Development Plan formed part of the bylaw and Development Permit Area 2 covered the hillside/upland area — where older and newer documents differ, the 2050 OCP and the 2025-updated Neighbourhood Plan govern.

Zoning: Zoning Bylaw 2020, No. 5000: Price lot potential from the zone AND the slope table, not the zone alone: the SHR minimum alone swings from 360 m² to 990 m² depending on slope, and HR doubles from 0.2 ha to 0.4 ha without a community water system.

Hillside Development Permit Area (Schedule D-5): a development permit is required for works including subdivision of land with 20% or greater slopes — slope measurement is a closing-condition item on hillside lots, not an afterthought.

Subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval, and ALR residences cannot be stratified — strata plans cause subdivision in the ALR (ALC Information Bulletin 09, s. 6; Strata Property Act, s. 239; Agricultural Land Commission Act, s. 21(1)). ALC residence caps: principal residence 500 m² or less total floor area; a secondary suite only within the principal residence; one additional residence of 90 m² or less (parcels 40 ha or less) or 186 m² or less (parcels over 40 ha).

Strata block — background if a strata lot is ever produced here: Form B (SPA s. 59) within 7 days of request, max $35 plus up to 25¢/page, disclosing fees, levies, CRF balance and insurance summary; depreciation reports every five years for stratas with five or more lots since July 1, 2024; minimum 10% CRF contribution since November 1, 2023; rental-restriction bylaws void since November 24, 2022; only 55+ age bylaws valid (SPA ss. 123.1/123.2, with the May 1, 2023 exemptions).

Chilliwack property taxes (city ground): a 5% late-payment penalty applies to taxes outstanding after July 2, 2026, and an additional 5% to taxes outstanding after August 4, 2026, per the City's property tax FAQ — a mid-year land buyer inherits whichever step has landed on an unpaid balance.

blocks.text: Good to know about Eastern Hillsides

items.t: Slope is a price variable here, not a footnote. The same SHR zone carries a 360 m² minimum on gentle ground and a 990 m² minimum on steep ground — two lots with the same zone and the same area can have completely different subdivision value once the slope table and the 20%-slope development-permit trigger are applied.

The heritage on these lots is wagon roads. The Neighbourhood Plan identifies the historic wagon road (Browlee Road) as a heritage asset to protect, and states wagon roads in the area include Nixon, Ruddock, Allan and Hinkley — a title and site-history check on an older hillside parcel can surface alignments a buyer would not expect.
There is no bus, no school, no shop inside the plan area — by the sources, not by impression. A land buyer here is buying a drive-for-everything lot.

blocks.text: Acreage and rural land in Eastern Hillsides

What acreage actually trades in Eastern Hillsides: individual fee-simple hillside parcels — large semi-serviced lots with single-family homes in the plan's early cells, under SHR (slope-table minimums), HR (0.2 ha / 0.4 ha) and RH (8 ha) zoning. The defining diligence fact for this area is not tenure or servicing — it is geotechnics: steep slopes, identified hazard areas, and the Marble Hill slide / moratorium ground.
The ground in Eastern Hillsides

items.t: Fee-simple parcels are the acreage form: An Eastern Hillsides acreage purchase is a fee-simple title purchase: no strata corporation, no Form B, no strata fee — City zoning, the slope table, development-permit conditions and any geotechnical covenants on title govern.
Hobby vs working-farm ground: Whether a north-edge parcel carries farm use is a parcel-level check (ALR status, zoning, BC Assessment class).

Serviced vs unserviced ground: The HR zone minimum itself turns on servicing: 0.2 ha with a community water system, 0.4 ha in all other cases — so servicing is a lot-potential fact, not just a utility fact.

blocks.text: Streets, schools and getting around Eastern Hillsides

items.t: Municipality: City of Chilliwack, BC. Eastern Hillsides is a hillside neighbourhood in southeast Chilliwack and a Neighbourhood Plan area, Schedule B4 of the Chilliwack 2050 Official Community Plan (Bylaw 2025, No. 5500).

Plan history: the Eastern Hillsides Neighbourhood Plan was adopted by Council in 2012 as part of the OCP, amended in 2017 to clarify development-approval requirements protecting future development from rock fall, landslide or earthflow with unstable conditions, and updated a third time in 2025 as part of the OCP update.

Where acreage actually trades: on the plan area's large-lot cells — the plan describes early development as large semi-serviced lots with single-family homes, with small-lot zoning in later cells, organized into development cells with unit allocations. The acreage ground is the HR / RH hillside ground, not the SHR / R3 small-lot cells.

Parks and trails serving the ground: Allan Creek Park, 51314 Rowanna Crescent; Forest Gate Park, 51442 Allan Road; Marble Hill Natural Area, 7515 Marble Hill Road; Allan Creek Trail; Chilliwack Community Forest, 51642 Allan Road; and the Elk Mountain Trail, all City-listed. No City recreation centre and no library branch is inside the plan area — the nearest recreation centre is Cheam Leisure Centre, 45501 Market Way, in Sardis, and the nearest library is Chilliwack Library, 45860 First Avenue.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect acreage buyers in Eastern Hillsides

items.t: Geotechnical rules: steep slopes, main watercourses and ravines cross the plan area and the plan identifies geotechnical hazard areas; the 2017 plan amendments were made specifically to protect future development from rock fall, landslide or earthflow with unstable conditions, and Council directed an expanded Marble Hill development moratorium area in 2017 after continuing ground movement was reported. The City's Greenspace Plan identifies the lower and upper Marble Hill slide areas as undevelopable lands. Get the property's geotechnical reports and any covenants on title before pricing or removing subjects, and check whether the lot sits in the moratorium area before counting on subdivision or a build.

Hillside Development Permit Area: hillside lots are subject to the 2050 OCP's Hillside Development Permit Area (Schedule D-5), under which a development permit is required for works including subdivision of land with 20% or greater slopes — slope measurement is a closing-condition item, not an afterthought. Heritage note in the same plan: the historic wagon road (Browlee Road) is identified as a heritage asset to protect; wagon roads in the area include Nixon, Ruddock, Allan and Hinkley.

If a strata purchase is made elsewhere (redirect case): the BC strata block applies — Form B diligence; depreciation reports on a 5-year cycle for stratas with 5+ lots since July 1, 2024; minimum 10% CRF contribution since November 1, 2023; rental-restriction bylaws void since November 24, 2022; only 55+ age bylaws valid (SPA ss.123.1/123.2, May 1, 2023 exemptions). None of it applies to an Eastern Hillsides fee-simple acreage purchase itself.

blocks.text: Good to know about Eastern Hillsides

items.t: Marble Hill is two facts at once: a named slope area inside the plan and a slide area the City calls undevelopable: The Greenspace Plan identifies the lower and upper Marble Hill slide areas as undevelopable lands, and Council directed an expanded development moratorium there in 2017 after continuing ground movement was reported. "Marble Hill" in a listing is a geotechnical diligence trigger, not just a view descriptor.

The wagon roads are a heritage layer on hillside title work: The Neighbourhood Plan identifies the historic wagon road (Browlee Road) as a heritage asset to protect, and names Nixon, Ruddock, Allan and Hinkley as wagon roads in the area — older hillside parcels can carry that history in their access and covenants.

Health care and daily services sit on the valley floor: Chilliwack General Hospital, 45600 Menholm Road, and the Chilliwack Urgent and Primary Care Centre, #104 – 7955 Evans Road (both Fraser Health), serve the city from below the hillsides — part of the real holding picture for acreage bought for its quiet.
